winner_rule: Before any pointer update, choose the candidate whose SHA-256(effect key) is lexicographically smallest; all candidates must name the same predecessor and frozen authority tuple.
replay_rule: After winner commit, a fresh LATEST containing the winner effect key is sufficient to classify both winner replay and loser replay as duplicate/suppressed and perform zero second logical advance.

mechanism_assessment.repository_transport_role: lightweight durable state/evidence transport only; no hosted runner, Codespaces, artifact/LFS/package, external model/API credit, or manual user execution is on the tested path
mechanism_assessment.tested_scope: Exactly two role-local orphan candidates sharing one predecessor, deterministic pre-commit arbitration, one permitted pointer update, and replay/loser suppression by fresh LATEST key detection. Concurrent writers, more than two candidates, and transport-level lost-before-server versus lost-after-server ambiguity remain untested.

exact_next_action: On the next valid invocation, execute exactly one recovery-indistinguishability probe for the unresolved transport boundary: model one attempted winner pointer write under two externally indistinguishable acknowledgement-loss worlds (not committed vs committed), then use only a fresh role-local LATEST read to classify server state before any replay. Prove committed-world replay yields zero second logical advance and uncommitted-world recovery permits at most one advance; if the connector surface cannot falsifiably represent both worlds, persist that exact capability blocker and an alternative role-local child. Do not start a second leaf.
